predecessors.name: Mali Empire
predecessors.text: Kaabu: 'modern northeastern Guinea-Bissau', with parts of the Gambia and the Casamance (Kolda), Koussanar and Koumpentoum; Fuladu is part of the former Kaabu

successors.name: Imamate of Futa Jallon
successors.text: north-eastern Guinea-Bissau, the heart of Kaabu with the capital Kansala

successors.name: Fuladu
successors.text: Fuladu, 'present-day Kolda and part of Tambacounda' and the upper Gambia

successors.name: Portuguese Guinea
successors.text: north-eastern Guinea-Bissau, the heart of Kaabu with the capital Kansala

ledger.x: 1537: Kaabu becomes independent of the Mali Empire.
1867: Fuladu breaks away under Alfa Molo.
1867: the Kaabu heartland passes to the Fula of Futa Jallon.

wars.name: Fula-Mandinka wars against Kaabu (Soninke-Marabout Wars)
wars.outcome: From 1776 the Torodbe state in the Futa Djallon "launched a jihad against non-Muslim states in the region, particularly Kaabu"; Kaabu repulsed Fula armies at Berekolong until the 1860s, when Futa Jallon and rebel Fula from Kaabu (Alfa Molo) took Kansala.

wars.name: Battle of Kansala
wars.outcome: Victory of Futa Jallon: Kansala was surrounded for one to three months, held for eleven days, and destroyed on 24 May 1867; Alfa Molo established Fuladu.

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier, only the countries and districts the kingdom lay in.
